newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie in hospital, soccer trial suspended.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie in hospital, soccer trial suspended.

text.p: Bernard Tapie, the fallen French tycoon and ex-soccer boss, was rushed from jail to hospital overnight after coming down with a mild heart problem, emergency care workers said on Wednesday.

Tapie, imprisoned nearly four months ago for fixing a soccer match and currently on trial for embezzling money from his former Marseille soccer club, woke up during the night complaining of chest pains and breathing difficulties.
But his illness might simply be due to stress from the trial, a spokesman for local ambulance services said.
Court officials announced that the 54-year-old Tapie's trial would be suspended until Thursday morning, at the earliest, due to his absence.
Tapie's attorney Yves Lienard said he was being treated in a coronary care unit at a hospital in Aix-en-Provence, southern France.
"His condition has improved this morning. He is willing to return to court as soon as he is discharged," Lienard said.
Tapie, a rags-to-riches businessman, pursued a promising career as a politician before ending up in jail as bankrupt prisoner 265 449G.
He has been on trial since May 12 on charges of embezzling 100 million francs ($17.5 million) from the Marseille team.

He was jailed after the French supreme court upheld his eight-month sentence for bribing players of league rival Valenciennes to give Marseille an easy game days before Marseille beat AC Milan in the 1993 European Cup final.
Nineteen other soccer figures are standing trial along with Tapie in the Marseille case, which opened on May 12 and is expected to last another two weeks.
He faces a five-year sentence if convicted on the charges of swindling, misusing corporate funds and falsifying documents between 1987 and 1993.
